title: Face Wall Generator
subtitle: Repeatable grids for checking face detectors
description: Tile a folder of face pictures into a seeded grid. Optionally crop faces with OpenCV’s YuNet detector before building the wall.
longDescription: A pip-installable Python CLI for building test images with known face counts and grid positions. Seeded selection makes layouts repeatable; optional YuNet face cropping prepares ordinary photos first. The repository includes public-domain portrait samples.
features: Seeded layouts with configurable rows and columns
results: Repeatable test grids with known face positions
why: Checking a face detector needs pictures where you already know the answer: how many faces, and where. Photos from the wild don't come with one, so this tool prints the answer key before the exam. It started as a test rig for the vision work at Infortrend.
gains: Handy in regression tests: the same seed and the same faces always give the same wall, so a detector's score changes only when the detector does. It needs only NumPy and headless OpenCV, so it runs in containers and CI, and the YuNet model ships inside the package.
lessons: Without cropping, a half-length portrait squeezed into a 72 px tile becomes a tiny person and a lot of background, hence --crop-faces.
Public-domain photos still show people with personality rights, so the samples are test data, not advert material.
